key_insight: All three URANS turbulence models capture key start-up behavior, but RSM better resolves trailing-edge and draft-tube frequency content by consistently capturing turbulence anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Computationally tractable start-up simulations can support variable-speed pump-turbine design as frequent start-stop cycles increase fatigue-loading concerns.
method: Simulate a linear start-up of a variable-speed reversible pump-turbine using transient CFD.
Compare k–ω SST, EARSM, and RSM within a URANS framework.
Assess torque, mass flow, and frequency content at blade edges and in the draft tube.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate torque, mass flow, and leading-edge blade-passing frequency content for all models, with substantially better trailing-edge and draft-tube spectral resolution using RSM.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative errors or computational costs, limiting assessment of the accuracy–cost trade-off.
paper_title: Transient CFD simulation of a linear start-up of a variable speed reversible pump-turbine
